issues.body: The prior finding is not fixed. `if any(entry[0][0] in FLOW_WORDS for entry in lists)` checks only the first token of each `;`/`&`-delimited list. The later `commands.extend(split_on(list_tokens, "&&"))` can still record commands after a flow-control command that occurs later in that same list. For example, with PyYAML proven in a separate RUN, `RUN true && exit 0 && jq --version` is accepted: the list begins with `true`, splitting records `["jq", "--version"]`, but `exit 0` terminates the shell before jq and the build remains green. `exec true` gives the same bypass. The new `deps-flow.Dockerfile` fixture uses `RUN set -eux; exit 0; jq --version`, where `exit` begins its semicolon-delimited list, so it passes even if the vulnerable post-`&&` path remains.
issues.fix_hint: Reject a RUN when a flow-control word begins any command produced after splitting an and-or list at `&&`, before recording any probes from that RUN. Add non-vacuous fixtures with the other dependency genuinely proven and `RUN true && exit 0 && jq --version` plus the analogous `exec true` form, asserting rejection and that jq is named.
issues.title: Flow control after && still permits unreachable probes

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-3 major remains unchanged: flow-control rejection still examines only the first token of each semicolon/ampersand-delimited list, before that list is split at `&&`. A later `exit` or `exec` can therefore make a recorded probe unreachable while the RUN succeeds. The added test still covers only `exit` at the start of a list, so it does not exercise the reported bypass. Progress is stagnant.
